paragraphs: Shabbat 30a relates a question put to R' Tanchum of Noy: may one extinguish a lamp for a sick person on Shabbat? Hyman describes him as opening with a teaching of Rav Yehudah in Rav's name and delivering a long discourse. He concludes, “Regarding the question I asked before you, a lamp is called a lamp,” etc. Hyman infers that he served as his town's judge and preacher.

notes.text: The supplied לעולא differs from the primary לעילא; no person named Ulla is introduced in the checked passage. באישא is the sick person, not an evil. The discourse begins on30a and concludes on30b. The exact supplied wording remains a source question.

No new primary scalar was returned. The earlier Shabbat 30a–b consultation with לעילא is inherited beside supplied לעולא, without treating a digital reading as proof of a vav/yod transcription-history error. No separate Ulla is introduced. באישא denotes the sick person. The supplied דשאילנא is now preserved as the first-person question I asked before you, rather than silently changed to passive. The final lamp quotation remains abbreviated, and Hyman's town-judge/preacher inference is attributed. Full supplied Rav Yehudah/Rav remain full; the uninspected Tanchum title remains R'.

Hyman's print (vol. III, p. 1243) and the consulted Shabbat 30a read לעילא where the supplied Hebrew has לעולא. The passage opens with an anonymous question and then a challenge to Solomon. It invokes teachings of Rav Yehudah in Rav's name later in the discourse. Shabbat 30b and Hyman's print both retain the first-person wording, “the question I asked before you.” The fuller lamp comparison remains outside Hyman's abbreviated quotation.
